oil.summary: Crude surged sharply on Tuesday, with WTI settling at $90.82/bbl (+5.89%) and Brent at $95.43/bbl (+5.46%), as Strait of Hormuz disruptions dominated flow. Two Saudi tankers were attacked in the Strait, Iran signaled its oil blockade would persist until strikes cease, and a tanker was separately struck near Oman — collectively threatening a critical artery for global supply. Russian production meanwhile hit its lowest since 2009 under combined pressure from Western sanctions and Ukrainian drone strikes on refinery infrastructure, forcing Moscow to import jet fuel. A weekly API draw of 2.6 million barrels added tightness on the demand side. RBOB gasoline was a notable outlier, falling 8.07% on the day despite crude strength — the divergence warrants monitoring. The $100/bbl threshold is firmly back in market conversation.
drivers: Strait of Hormuz blockade and tanker attacks on Saudi vessels driving acute supply-risk premium
Russian oil production at lowest since 2009; Ukraine strikes disrupting refinery output and forcing fuel imports
API crude inventory draw of 2.6 million barrels reinforcing tight physical market; $100/bbl level back in focus

gas.summary: Natural gas markets tightened on both sides of the Atlantic. Henry Hub edged up 0.61% to $2.953/MMBtu, while TTF jumped 3.39% to €72.175/MWh — a 25.51% gain over the past month — as Hormuz-related LNG disruptions continue to squeeze spot availability. Asia spot LNG prices reached their highest since the 2026 winter as buyers scrambled for cargoes amid stalled Hormuz transits. Russia has meanwhile doubled its dark-fleet LNG shipping capacity in nine months to sustain Arctic LNG 2 exports to Asia under sanctions. Treasury Secretary Bessent offered a longer-term counterpoint, claiming Gulf producers could route around the Strait within two years, though the market gave that timeline little near-term credit.
drivers: Hormuz blockage forcing Asian LNG buyers into spot market competition, pushing prices to five-month highs
TTF up 25.5% over the past month as European gas market absorbs supply rerouting and geopolitical risk premium
Russia doubling dark-fleet LNG tanker capacity to sustain sanctioned Arctic LNG 2 exports to Asian buyers

power.summary: The power and carbon complex was relatively quiet compared to oil and gas. EU carbon EUAs edged up just 0.47% to $79.00/EUA, with the weekly move slightly negative at -0.70%, suggesting the carbon market has not yet fully repriced the energy-cost surge seen in TTF. The Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant's continued reliance on diesel generators amid ongoing conflict adds a diffuse risk to European grid stability. On the infrastructure side, U.S. energy storage installations hit a record high in Q2 as grid operators sought reliability buffers — consistent with the broader lithium price rally. A two-week blackout in Gary, Indiana served as a pointed reminder of domestic grid vulnerability. Solar buildout in emerging markets continues at record pace but provided no immediate price catalyst today.
drivers: EU EUAs largely range-bound despite surging TTF, suggesting carbon-energy spread compression worth monitoring
Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant on diesel backup amid conflict, adding tail risk to European power grid stability
U.S. Q2 energy storage installations hit record high; Gary, Indiana blackout highlights persistent grid infrastructure gaps
